messages.subject: Error in get_pwet
parts:
Hello NicheMappers,

I'm having a quick play with the function get_pwet for computing % surface area acting as a free water exchanger.

If I use the example:
test<-get_pwet(cut.known = 1, E_tot = 0.344 / 60 / 1000, E_cut = 0.108 / 60 / 1000, T_b = 25, RHin = 30, vel = 0.0021)

I'm met with an error:

Error in get_pwet(cut.known = 1, E_tot = 0.344/60/1000, E_cut = 0.108/60/1000,  :
  object 'e_air' not found

I've checked the function's source code and 'e_air' isn't a parameter the user needs to specify so I'm wondering where this needs to come from? Should I have run a function previously which computes e_air, prior to running get_pwet?

Many thanks
Simon

Hi Simon!

I have checked the function and e_air seems related to respiratory water loss (line 164 in: https://github.com/mrke/NicheMapR/blob/master/R/get_pwet.R). Since in that example E_resp is provided (observed respiratory evaporative water loss rate, g/s), you can set resp.known = 1, and the function will work without errors or warnings. Besides, you can set manually e_air (and e_lung!), and the function will work too.

Hopefully, Mike will be able to give you a better and more detailed response.

Hope this helps! Good luck!

Cheers,
Urtzi

messages.author: 54d4981d6bf68eaf
messages.subject: Re: Error in get_pwet
parts:
Hi!

You are right. You are not providing E_resp directly. However, I think that all E_* parameters have a default value (e.g. E_resp= 0.0371 / 60 / 1000) that are used by the function. If you just type get_pwet in the console, you will see that the default input parameters are:

function (cut.known = 0, resp.known = 0, eye.known = 0, vent.known = 0,
    press.known = 0, A_tot.known = 0, E_tot = 0.344/60/1000,
    E_cut = 0.108/60/1000, E_resp = 0.0371/60/1000, E_eye = 0.199/60/1000,
    mass.g = 26.7, A_tot = 0.00894, fcond = 0.25, feye = 0.002,
    eye_frac = 0.58, T_b = 25, T_s = 25 - 0.001, T_a = 25 - 0.002,
    vel = 0.0021, RHex = 100, RHin = 30, E_O2 = 15, RQ = 0.766,
    M_1 = 0.013, M_2 = 0.8, M_3 = 0.0038, V_O2_STP = M_1 * mass.g^M_2 *
        10^(M_3 * T_b)/3600/1000, T_ref_O2 = 30, V_air_STP = V_O2_STP/(0.2094 *
        E_O2/100), rho_flesh = 1000, T_ref_vent = 30, T_A = 8817,
    T_AL = 50000, T_AH = 90000, T_L = 279, T_H = 306, alt = 0,
    bp = 101325)

So, even if you run the function like this: get_pwet(resp.known=1), you will get an "answer", based on those input parameters. Does it make sense?

The issue you came across (when running the function with resp.known=0) could be somehow important if you don't have knowledge on the actual respiratory water loss of your species, and you would like to estimate it with this function. However, since the code to compute E_resp is already there, it should be relatively easy to fix by including e_air and e_lung as arguments to the function

All the best,
Urtzi

If anyone's able to help, I have some extra related questions with regards to get_pwet and the regular ectotherm() function.

Within NicheMapR::ectotherm() the parameter 'skinwet' is required (recently renamed to pct_wet). If this value isn't available, it's possible to estimate it with the function get_pwet().

However, there are arguments within 'get_pwet' related, presumably, to the microclimatic conditions experienced by the organism (e.g. relative humidity, wind speed etc) along with a handful of physiological arguments (e.g. T_b). 

My first question is: how can 'skinwet' be computed prior to running micro_global() or ectotherm(), given that Tb is an argument within the get_pwet function? To estimate an animal's Tb you'd need to first run ectotherm(). Yet ectotherm() requires the skinwet parameter in order to generate an accurate estimate of Tb. It seems pretty circular to me and I can't think my way out of the problem.

My additional questions are:

1. how sensitive is get_pwet is to the initial Tb of the organism (as specified by 'T_b' within get_pwet)? If it's mostly irrelevant, I guess a ballpark Tb could be used to generate an estimate of % skin acting as a free water exchanger?
2. Are the environmental arguments within get_pwet microclimate estimates from NicheMapR::micro_global? i.e. are they location specific?

Thanks again!
Simon

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Error in get_pwet
parts:
Hi Simon,

I'm still finalising and documenting all the ectotherm model related material. It's really a beta version right now. Part of what I still have to do is document the get_pwet function better including some examples. I'll get to this pretty soon - but for now, to answer your question above - you need to think of pct_wet as a parameter. It is the fraction the total surface area is multiplied by when working out the cutaneous water loss. To estimate it, you need experimental data on actual water loss at a known Tb. Then you can predict it at any other Tb (and air temp, wind speed, vapour pressure combination).

Make sense? You can read a bit more about it in the appendix to Kearney and Porter 2004 (attached).

All the best,
Mike

Hi Simon and Urtzi,

I haven't quite finished this function - probably shouldn't have put it in the package yet! I seemed to have missed out on a line:
    e_air <- WETAIR(db = T_a, rh = RHin)$e
This was the cause for the error. The value e_air is the vapour pressure of the air that the animal is breathing in. Also, e_lung was missing
    e_lung <- WETAIR(db = T_b, rh = 100)$e
This is the vapour pressure of the exhaled air (assuming it is saturated).

I've just fixed it and pushed it to github. I'll go through and finalise this function in the next couple of weeks I hope and make sure it works properly.

All the best,
Mike
